objective: Create app/services/pdflib_shim.py (a vendored minimal pure-stdlib PDF writer implementing the C5 doc API: open/add_page/add_text/save -> bytes, header %PDF-1.4, one page object per add_page, computed xref, trailer, %%EOF) and app/services/labels.py (the exact C4 EN/DE label tables), each with passing unit tests.

concepts: minimal PDF file structure (header, page objects, xref table, trailer)

inputs: frozen contract C4 (label key sets + exact strings)

frozen_contracts.spec: label tables for pdf generation: LABELS = {'en': {customer, period, title, metric, value}, 'de': {Kunde, Periode, Titel, Kennzahl, Wert}} — exact key set {customer, period, title, metric, value}; renderer must not hardcode label strings outside these tables.

vendored pdflib_shim module at app/services/pdflib_shim.py exposing: open() -> doc, doc.add_page(), doc.add_text(x, y, text, size=10), doc.save() -> bytes — a ~40-line pure-stdlib wrapper producing a minimal valid PDF (header %PDF-1.4, pages, xref, trailer).

non_goals: no report rendering logic here (that is T03)
no changes to existing app files
implementation_constraints: save() output MUST start with b'%PDF' and end with a trailer/%%EOF so a downstream page-count check can run on bytes
xref offsets must be computed from the bytes actually written (no hardcoded offsets)
labels.py exposes LABELS as a plain dict; no imports from anywhere else in the app
tests use plain unittest like tests/test_export.py

acceptance_tests.description: open -> one add_page -> add_text -> save() returns bytes starting b'%PDF' containing one page object and ending with %%EOF
two add_page calls make save() return two page objects in the bytes (the test counts /Page dicts == 2, no /Pages confusion)
the test asserts the LABELS key set is exactly {customer, period, title, metric, value} for both langs and LABELS['de']['customer'] == 'Kunde'
a missing label key access raises KeyError (no silent default) — LABELS['en']['nope'] raises

failure_cases.expected_behavior: the document still renders a page; save() returns bytes with a valid header (empty content stream is legal)
xref offsets remain correct (computed, not hardcoded); test asserts the last page is present

handoff.notes: the shim's byte layout is the only surface T03 depends on; if xref computation proves hard, the fallback is a simpler 'objects written in order' layout — but save() must still start with %PDF and keep page objects countable.

warnings.detail: minimal PDF structure is hand-rolled; xref offset bugs are the likely failure
warnings.rationale: stdlib has no PDF writer; the shim is a 40-line wrapper by platform-team convention
